title: Transient surge breather and telemetry-anchored circuit fuse
author: Amira Khan
ci_status: pass (one flaky integration test retried and green)
release_notes: Hotfix: add transient surge-breather admission and telemetry-anchored circuit fuse to reduce SLO breaches during short regional traffic spikes. Backward compatible; default disabled via config flag.
description:
Motivation: We saw multiple short spikes (bursts of 10-30s) that caused rapid circuit flips and SLO violations in regional routers. Existing load-shedding thresholds were too coarse, and KV-preserve logic delayed eviction in ways that amplified downstream pressure. This PR introduces a lightweight 'surge breather' admission gate plus a telemetry-anchored circuit fuse that uses SLO-drift signals (p50/p95 delta and error-rate derivative) to open a soft circuit with graceful degradation and bounded retry cooling.

What this does: Adds a transient admission gate (surge breather) that buffers microbursts for a configurable short window (default 15s) to flatten token peaks without full eviction. The circuit fuse observes an aggregated SLO drift metric and uses a smoothed exponential cooloff to avoid rapid reopen cycles. When the fuse opens it triggers: (1) soft deny with informative structured response for compatible clients, (2) an optional degrade-to-compact-model route for customers with tiered fallbacks, and (3) telemetry annotation so downstream observability can attribute SLO debt.

Implementation details: single-string summary of changes below. Key runtime changes live under runtime/shedder and runtime/circuit: the breather is implemented as a token-budgeted short FIFO queue that cooperates with the request scheduler; if the queue fills we fall back to existing tenant-priority trimmers. The circuit fuse subscribes to slo_signals stream and computes a bounded derivative using a 3-window EWMA; fuse state is persisted in-memory with optional sticky hint in kv/lease for cross-process reconciliation. Configuration: feature flag enabled by config.shepherd.surge_breather.enabled=false by default; can be toggled per-region and per-tenant.

Testing & verification: added unit tests for queue behavior and circuit cooloff math, integration test that replays a recorded burst trace to ensure we reduce peak qps by ~40% and avoid >1s p95 regressions. Ran canary in staging in region-eu-west for 3 hours against synthetic spike generator and observed no circuit flip oscillation and 18% reduction in mitigation-induced evictions.

Operational notes and rollout plan: staged rollout (off by default): 1) feature flag gated — enable in staging; 2) enable in low-traffic region with telemetry on; 3) progressive ramp to high-traffic regions with daily checkpoints. Metrics to monitor: surge_breather.queue_fill_ratio, surge_breather.drop_count, slo_fuse.state_transitions, slo_fuse.cooldown_seconds, tenant_eviction_rate. Runbook: if unexpected increase in client 429s or unexplained SLO regressions, toggle config.shepherd.surge_breather.enabled=false and the fuse will gracefully transition to closed state after current cooloff.

Related work: ENG-2805 (diagnose regional burst flips), ENG-2812 (tiered fallback routing).

Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration test, [x] staging canary, [x] observability dashboards updated, [x] docs updated with operational guidance.

review_comments: Diego Rios: Nice minimal design. A couple of questions: how do we avoid tenant unfairness when the breather queues across tenants? Can we tag queue slots by tenant weight?
Amira Khan: We allocate token budgets per-tenant proportional to current SLA weight; added token accounting in surge_breather.go and callouts in docs. See commit b2b6c7d.
Jun Park: The EWMA window feels tight; can we have a guard so derivative spikes from short-lived noise don't trip the fuse?
Amira Khan: Added a min-duration floor (3s) and a derivative deadband, documented in the code comments and config. Also added unit tests to cover the deadband case.
Sofia Patel: CI flaked on integration test under heavy CPU. Reran and it's green. Approving to merge after small doc tweak.
